newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African trade data to take on new format.
newsitem.headline: S.African trade data to take on new format.

text.p: South Africa's Customs and Excise Department said on Friday it planned to release trade data in the near future which would exclude other countries in the region.

The department's current data includes trade statistics from the BLNS countries -- Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Swaziland -- which economists have complained makes it difficult to guage the state of South Africa's current account balance.
Botswana's figures in particular, which mainly consist of diamond exports, often result in South African trade figures being highly volatile on a month-to-month basis.

Customs and Excise assistant director of statistics Jack Heyns told Reuters that while no timeframe was envisaged for the new format, it was hoped that they would be available by the second half of this year.
Heyns said that the department was currently developing programmes which would separate the data, a process which he said was expected to take about two to three months.
